messages:
incident-bot: Pager: geo-dns-anomaly detected (high SERVFAIL/NX) for eu-central endpoints. Severity: P1. Pages: #incidents + @sre-omar oncall.

sre-omar: I see the spike on the EU resolver error metric starting ~6m ago. 503s rising on inference-proxy layer. Triage in progress.

net-kate: quick check: `dig @1.1.1.1 api.eu.redwood.ai` -> SERVFAIL intermittently. `dig @4.2.2.2` returns fine. Route53 answers OK. Looks like Cloudflare resolver path is flapping for some prefixes.

infra-sam: no infra deploys. Egress NAT gateways show retransmits to CF resolver IPs. Could be rate-limiting or transient network blackholing.

pm-luca: customer comms? were getting support DMs. Need an ETA for mitigation.

support-neha: started triage with affected accounts, ~7 tickets so far. Some customers reported inference failures and SDK retries. Rough impact: ~3.5% of EU requests failing, concentrated in eu-central AZ.

oncallbot: Handoff scheduled: @sre-omar -> @net-kate in 8 minutes. Also creating incident bridge.

sre-omar: quick mitigation idea: swap geo-dns policy for eu-central to use route53-primary + cf-secondary, and reduce CF weight to 0 until stable. That should steer queries away from CF resolvers quickly.

net-kate: I'll run the change. Command: 
```
geo-dns apply --region eu-central --policy "route53_only" --ttl 30
```
Applying now, will post when done.

infra-sam: applied. `geo-dns get eu-central` shows policy=route53_only, TTL=30. Note: short TTL so propagation should be quick but may cause cache churn.

sre-omar: monitoring error rate... good sign: errors dropping from 3.5% -> 0.8% over 4m. Latency bump observed due to cache misses.

incident-bot: Automatic rollback disabled for this mitigation. Manual approval required before reverting.

net-kate: opened ticket with Cloudflare (CF-INC-17902) including packet captures and dig traces. Also pinged AWS support; Route53 appears healthy.

dns-bot: probe-runner logs: started continuous probes to 1.1.1.1, 4.2.2.2, and 8.8.8.8 from eu-egress. Logging results to s3://redwood-incidents/1730012345/probes.csv

support-neha: customer update posted: "Were aware of DNS resolution errors impacting EU endpoints. We've temporarily routed DNS traffic to an alternate provider; we're monitoring and will follow up with details."

pm-luca: good. Please capture timeline for postmortem: when spike started, mitigation time, error delta, customer impact list.

net-kate: capturing timeline now. Preliminary: t0=1730012345 spike start, mitigation push t1=1730012460, errors reduced by ~75% at t1+4m.

infra-sam: added a short-term alert: if EU resolver SERVFAIL ratio >1.5% for 2m, page SRE. Also increased probe frequency to 30s for the next hour.

sre-omar: note for postmortem: consider adding resolver-specific panels to the Console: per-resolver SERVFAIL, NX, RTT, and upstream packet loss.

net-kate: CF replied acknowledging the ticket, investigating possible upstream peering congestion. Asked for our packet captures and ASN traces. Uploaded captures to the CF portal.

dns-bot: automated summary: captured 420 probe failures to Cloudflare resolvers between t0 and t1. Attached probe hashes: sha256:ab12...

support-neha: customers on the thread confirm reduction in errors after our mitigation. One reported increased cold-starts but acceptable.

oncallbot: Reminder: if mitigation remains >45m, schedule rotation for extended incident handling and assign postmortem owner.

pm-luca: assigning postmortem owner: @net-kate. Please prepare RCA and runbook updates.

net-kate: will do. Immediate next steps: await CF root cause, keep route53-only for 1h, then gradually reintroduce CF at 20% increments while we watch 1m SERVFAIL metric.

sre-omar: agreed. Add a runbook step to check egress path MTU and peering for anomalies; we saw retransmits.

incident-bot: Incident status -> monitoring. Summary: EU resolver path to Cloudflare experienced transient failures causing customer-facing DNS errors; geo-dns failover to Route53 reduced impact. Postmortem owner: net-kate.

net-kate: handing back to regular oncall. Thanks all, good triage and comms. :clap:
